column5: M's unit takes the small enemy facing it and his dot becomes mine; when the enemy kills it, A's revive brings it back into a front cell and its Place takes the next small enemy facing it. He answers by keeping strength 3+ units in that front cell.
column6: BOARD: M change (front cells) + A revive

column5: M discards a card for its discard effect, A's recycle brings it back to hand to discard or play again. Card value, not a base: it changes no front cell by itself.

H discards a big unit from hand (its discard effect acts), then A's revive places it from the discard pile into a free front cell for little supply. The enemy can't touch my discard pile, so between the two cards he can only fill the facing front cell to cancel the dot. Needs revive to take units that were discarded, not only units that died.

A's holder in a front cell dies and its Death deals 3 to the enemy facing it; when I next place a unit in that lane, H's recycle brings it back into a free middle-row cell, ready to step up and die again. He answers by not killing it, which leaves my dot.

R's rider sits on A's front holder; when the enemy kills the holder its Death deals 3 to the enemy facing it and the rider drops into the cell, so the cell needs two kills and his attacker dies. He answers by silencing the holder or killing it from a column where the 3 damage hits nothing.
column6: BOARD: R attach (rider drops) + A lastwords (facing)

column5: A's lastwords unit in a front cell is killed, its Death acts; R's revive returns it into that cell, its Place acts and it can die for its Death again. Revive is only an extra of R, so the second half is rare in the deck.

S's allyplay unit stands in a back cell; A's token maker fills my front cells and each token counts as a placed unit, so S deals 1 damage to the enemy facing each token. He answers by killing the allyplay unit with a Ranged unit; tokens are only an extra of A.

One A card puts several small units in my camp; S's countboard units give +1 supply or +1 strength for each other unit of mine, so the tokens pay for big units in that lane. He answers with an area hit on the tokens.
column6: BOARD: A tokens + S countboard (supply per unit)

column5: T's fight card makes the enemy facing my I unit strike it; the I unit survives the hit and its hurt text acts on my turn, not his. He answers by killing the hurt unit outright or silencing it.
T's fight card makes my 5+ strength I unit strike a chosen enemy, so any enemy dies. Mostly bigger numbers.

D's unit with Death "add a 1-supply Guard card to hand" holds a front cell; T's offering lets it die for supply, and the Guard card refills the cell next turn. He can kill it first, which still gives me the card.
column6: LIBRARY KEEP offering+create; BOARD: D create (front cells)

column5: Each T damage spell also sets off D's spellpay units. Bigger numbers; spellpay is only an extra of D.

G's unit in the front-middle cell strikes every enemy in its reach; T's fight card makes it strike without using its attack, so all three facing front cells are hit and it can still attack this round. Before the fight card he can only attack the G unit, which strikes first or survives with its defence.
column6: LIBRARY KEEP fight+strikes; BOARD: G strikes (all in reach)

column5: T's fight card makes P's big unit strike the enemy facing it; the damage beyond its defence hits the unit behind, so the holder and its replacement die in one action without P's attack. He answers by killing or weakening the P unit first.
column6: LIBRARY KEEP fight+strikes; BOARD: P overkill

column5: Each T unit that dies gives my other units strength; when P's unit reaches 5 it holds its dot even with an enemy facing it. Needs a few deaths first; he answers with his own 5+ unit facing it.
column6: LIBRARY KEEP deathfeed+bigstrength; BOARD: P bigstrength (holds dot, NEW RULE)

column5: T's unit whose Place strikes the enemy facing it is taken back to hand by K and placed again in another front cell, striking again. Costs supply each time; he answers by killing it before it returns.
column6: BOARD: T fight (front cells) + K returnhand

column5: T's offering lets my unit die for supply; K's revive brings it back and its Place acts again. Two gains from one unit; he can't stop it, but it changes no front cell by itself.
Extra supply lets me cast a spell almost every turn, so E's spellpay units fire more. Bigger numbers only.

Q's push moves the enemy cancelling my I unit's dot back; at round start the dot is uncancelled and the I unit gives +1 supply in that lane. He answers by moving a unit back into the facing cell before round end.
column6: BOARD: Q push (front cells, NEW RULE) + I supply (dots)

column5: While I's unit is in the lane his deploys cost 1 more, and Q's ping deals 1 to each enemy placed facing my unit: refilling a lost front cell costs more and a 1-defence unit dies. He answers by placing a bigger unit or killing one of the two.
column6: BOARD: I hand (supply per lane) + Q ping (facing)

column5: N gives my front I units a shield each round start; each enemy hit breaks the shield instead of killing, the I unit survives and its hurt text acts. He answers by silencing or by not attacking, which leaves my dot.
column6: BOARD: N shield (round start) + I hurt

column5: B's offering Place lets my cheap holder die and the 5+ strength I unit goes into its cell for less, a round early and without opening the dot. He can't stop it; it is mostly a cheaper big unit.
column6: BOARD: B offering (placed into freed cells, NEW RULE) + I bigstrength

column5: B's swap moves the hurt I unit back and a fresh one forward without using moves. Little more than moving.
L's silence takes his shields and can't-be-targeted text away from the units around it, then E's damage spell kills them. He answers by moving the unit or placing a new protected one.
column6: BOARD: L silence (cells around) + E spelldmg

column5: L's silence removes his shields and protections; Q's 1-damage pings then finish small front holders. He answers by refilling with units of 2+ defence.

L's unit whose Place silences the facing enemy goes back to hand with N's returnhand and is placed again to silence the new unit he placed. Returnhand is only an extra of N, and each placement costs supply.
L's unit whose Place takes strength from the facing enemy is returned by N and placed again, shrinking it for good each time. Same limits as above.
L's weakener in my front row gives the facing enemy -2 strength, so its hits no longer kill B's hurt units, which survive and act. He answers by attacking with a unit not facing the weakener.
M creates cards that were not in my deck; D's cheaper makes created cards cost 1 less, so two created holders fit in one lane's supply. Mostly cheaper cards; the enemy can't stop it.
D's extra draws feed M's discard effects. Card value only.
M takes or blocks enemy units, G strikes harder; neither changes what the other does on this board.
M's junk and change and P's big strikes don't set each other off; together they only add numbers.
K returns M's unit whose Place takes a small enemy to hand; I place it again facing another small enemy and take it too. He answers by keeping strength 3+ units facing my front cells.
column6: LIBRARY KEEP change+returnhand; BOARD: M change (front cells)

column5: K returns M's unit whose Place creates a card, and it creates another. Card value only, paid in supply.
H's recycle brings E's spent damage spells back to hand, so the same removal kills the next front holder he places. Each recycle is a card, and the enemy can't stop it, but it changes no rule.

H's cheap ping spells each set off E's spellpay unit: 1 damage from the spell and 1 to the enemy facing the spellpay unit, so two cheap spells clear a 2-defence canceller. He answers by killing the spellpay unit.

E's spellpay unit hidden in a front cell holds its dot and can't be attacked or targeted, and its damage is not an attack so it stays hidden; each spell I cast deals 1 to the enemy facing it. He can only cancel the dot by facing it, and that unit takes the damage. Needs R to give hide to E's unit.
column6: BOARD: R hide (NEW RULE) + E spellpay (facing)

column5: An attached item gives my spells +1 damage. Bigger numbers and two named cards.
S's push moves his back-row Ranged unit into a front cell; my next spell deals 1 to every enemy in that front row. He can move it back with his own action; push is only an extra of S.
column6: LIBRARY KEEP spelldmg+push; BOARD: E spelldmg (rows)

column4: J's returnhand + D's draw or create Place
column5: J returns D's unit whose Place draws or creates cards, and I place it again for another draw. Card value paid with supply and actions; it holds no cell by itself.
column6: LIBRARY KEEP draw+returnhand; LIBRARY KEEP create+returnhand

column5: A round-start card adds a copy to hand and I discard it for a discard effect. Needs named cards; discard is only an extra of D.
C's offering lets D's front unit die for supply, and its Death adds a Guard card that refills the cell next turn. He can kill it first, which still gives me the card.
column6: LIBRARY KEEP create+offering; BOARD: D create (front cells)

column5: C's sacrifice lets D's unit die to kill the enemy facing it, and its Death gives a Guard card to take the cell back. The trade of units ends with my card in hand; he answers by refilling first.
O's offering lets D's unit die for supply and its Death adds a Guard card to hand. Same as with C; O's offering is only an extra.
My units' deaths grow F's others and J's revive brings the dead back to die again. Both are extras; mostly numbers.
C's sacrifice lets my unit die to kill an enemy; J's revive brings it back, its Place acts and it can be sacrificed again. Both are extras, so both cards must be drawn.

J returns C's line-of-3 front unit whose Place deals 1 to every enemy in its three columns, and I place it again to hit all three cancellers again. Costs supply each time; he answers with units of 2+ defence.

J takes my unit back to hand; it leaving the grid sets off O's leave cards, and placing it again makes its Place act again. Two effects from one action; he can't stop it, but it is value more than a cell.
J's copy places a copy of O's token maker in the free front cell beside it, and the copy's Place puts tokens again. Needs free cells; he answers with an area hit.
column6: BOARD: J copy (front row) + O tokens

column5: H discards a big unit and R's revive places it from the discard pile. Revive is only an extra of R and must take units that were discarded.

H's unit that deals 1 to the enemy facing it whenever I discard is hidden in a front cell by R: it holds the dot and can't be attacked, and each discard hits the enemy facing it. Needs R to give hide to H's unit.
column6: BOARD: R hide (NEW RULE) + H discard (facing)

column5: When I place a unit in the lane, H's recycle unit comes back into my middle row; if that counts as a placement, S's allyplay deals 1 to the enemy facing each. One deploy, two hits; he answers by killing the allyplay unit.
H's discarded unit is placed free into a front cell, one more unit for S's countboard. Bigger numbers.
column6: BOARD: H discard (placed when discarded, NEW RULE) + S countboard

column5: Q's fight card makes G's first-striking front unit strike a chosen enemy, which dies before it hits back. Fight is only an extra of Q.
Q's push moves enemies into his front row; G's unit in the front-middle cell then strikes all three facing front cells in one attack. He answers by moving one back out with his action.
Q's push moves an enemy into the cell behind his front holder; P's big unit strikes the holder and the rest kills the unit behind. He can move it out with one action before my attack.
K returns Q's unit whose Place deals 1 to each enemy in the lane, and I place it again to finish the wounded ones. Costs supply each time.

K marks the enemy front cell facing it, so his unit there must leave or die at round end; Q's unit deals 1 to any enemy placed or moved back into that cell. The cell stays empty unless he pays for a big unit or kills one of mine.
column6: BOARD: K kill (mark, NEW RULE) + Q ping (facing)

column5: A shielded G unit attacks twice and survives the hits back. Bigger numbers only.
B's swap puts G's attacker into the front cell without using its move. Only saves a move.
N's guard makes his attacks go to F's unit, which survives, acts with its hurt text, and is healed at round start. He answers by silencing or killing it in one hit.
column6: BOARD: N guard (nearest-target, NEW RULE) + F heal

column5: Shield and heal keep the same front holder alive. Both only add defence.
B's offering lets my unit die for supply or carry-over, and F's deathfeed grows my other units from the same death: one death pays twice. He can't stop it.
B's hurt unit survives a hit and acts; F's heal restores it at round start, so it can be hit and act again every round. He answers by killing it in one round.

R's rider gives P's front unit its strength and defence, lifting it to 5+, so it holds its dot even with an enemy facing it; when it dies the rider drops into the cell. He needs his own 5+ unit or a silence; his one action between the two cards rarely kills a big P unit.
column6: BOARD: R attach (NEW RULE) + P bigstrength (holds dot, NEW RULE)

column5: An attached item unlocks a second strike on P's front unit. Needs a named item.
R takes K's unit back to hand; placed again, its Place destroys another enemy. Mostly K's own plan; R's returnhand is an extra.
column6: LIBRARY KEEP returnhand+kill; BOARD: K kill (supply)

column5: S damages my own units for its gains; N's shield takes that damage, so the gain costs nothing. He can't stop it; selfhurt is only an extra of S.
N returns a unit and placing it again sets off S's allyplay. Costs an action and supply for one more trigger.
When my front unit dies, C's deathfeed gives my unit behind +1|+1 and steps it in; P's unit crossing 5 strength holds its dot even with an enemy facing it. Needs deaths first.
column6: LIBRARY KEEP bigstrength+deathfeed; BOARD: C deathfeed (NEW RULE) + P bigstrength (NEW RULE)

column5: C's sacrifice lets P's lastwords unit die: an enemy dies from the sacrifice and its Death acts too. Both are extras, so both cards must be drawn.

column4: O's offering of tokens + P's bigstrength
column5: O's tokens die for strength and push P's unit to 5. Mostly O's own plan plus numbers.

column4: P's big shapes vs O's tokens
column5: P's units take two or three cells each and O's tokens need free cells in the same 9-cell camp, so one fills the room the other needs.

O fills my front cells with tokens and puts units behind them; when he kills a token, C's deathfeed gives the unit behind +1|+1 and steps it into the cell at once. Killing my holder only brings a bigger one, and leaving it keeps my dot.
column6: BOARD: O tokens + C deathfeed (NEW RULE)

column5: O's cheap tokens are what C's sacrifice lets die to kill or hit an enemy: one cheap unit for one of his. He answers by placing units that are worth less than the trade.
B's offering lets my unit die for supply; K's revive brings it back and its Place acts again. He can't stop it; it changes no front cell by itself.
K's outright kill of his front unit grows B's unit's supply. Bigger numbers.
